## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Counterfactuals and potential outcomes. Every comparison is a claim about a world that did not happen. Then causal graphs: confounders, colliders, mediators, back-door reasoning. And why controlling for everything makes things worse. Finally the map for the rest of this half. Every design we meet closes a back door in a different way. You will draw each one before you hear what it is called.

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

First, teams. You are put into one, and it writes down its own ground rules today, while everybody still gets along. Who does what. What happens when somebody misses a deadline. How you settle a disagreement. One page, signed, handed in. Then your team's first job together. Each team draws a card carrying a real causal claim somebody is acting on — a board paper, a marketing deck, a widely shared post. Every card is broken differently. Draw the graph behind it, then name the failure in this morning's vocabulary. Then one team is drawn at random to defend its diagnosis while the room attacks, and we draw again as the clock allows. You will not know whether you are up. Card 3 is a collider and card 5 is a mediator. Those two are where the morning either landed or it did not.

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.

## Due

Your team's written ground rules — agreed and handed in today
